title: The Mahavamsa: or the Great Chronicle of Ceylon — Chapter 37, King Mahasena
date: 1950 edition of Geiger translation; chronicle is premodern
author_or_institution: Mahavamsa; Wilhelm Geiger translation; National Library of Sri Lanka digital copy
scope: Mahasena, Sanghamitta, sanctions against Mahavihara, abandonment/destruction narrative, Jetavana foundation
limitations: Mahavamsa is produced within the Mahavihara lineage and is openly hostile to its rivals; indispensable primary testimony but not a neutral description of factional motives

title: The ‘Fearless Mountain’ That (Almost) Disappeared: Looking for the History of the Abhayagiri-vihara in Sri Lanka
scope: Abhayagiri–Mahavihara rivalry, Chinese sources, transregional and tantric/Mahayana traces
limitations: Centres on Abhayagiri; it helps correct Mahavihara-source bias but should not be used to make Jetavana identical to Abhayagiri or to a timeless modern Mahayana bloc

title: Rewriting Buddhism: Pali Literature and Monastic Reform in Sri Lanka, 1157–1270
scope: Parakramabahu I, reform era, purification and unification of the Sangha in 1165, intellectual consequences
limitations: Medieval reform focus; use as callback/closure to Anuradhapura pluralism, not as direct evidence for fourth-century Jetavana

title: Flanked by Images of Our Buddha — Buddhism and Law, Chapter 7
author_or_institution: Cambridge University Press, Buddhism and Law
scope: Parakramabahu I's Gal Vihara monastic regulation and its durable legal-institutional significance
limitations: Legal-regulatory lens; does not by itself reconstruct all doctrinal currents or fourth-century monastic economics

title: Evolution of the dry zone water harvesting and management systems in Sri Lanka during the Anuradhapura Kingdom; a study based on ancient chronicles and lithic inscriptions
scope: Irrigation works, water revenues, taxes, grants of tanks/fields/water shares to monasteries and monks
limitations: Supports the institutional resource circuit and hydro-fiscal setting; it does not quantify a specific fiscal transfer caused by Mahasena's conflict

title: Ancient Water Management and Governance in the Dry Zone of Sri Lanka Until Abandonment, and the Influence of Colonial Politics during Reclamation
scope: Ownership/governance of irrigation in Anuradhapura, monastic grants and religious-purpose resource transfers
limitations: Water-governance focus and uneven epigraphic survival, especially for the fourth–seventh centuries

title: Buddhist Meditation Monasteries of Ancient Sri Lanka — comparison with Sacred City of Anuradhapura
author_or_institution: UNESCO World Heritage Centre / Sri Lanka tentative-list submission
scope: Mahavihara, Abhayagiri and Jetavana as major Anuradhapura monastic complexes and centres of education/social activity
limitations: Heritage synthesis, not a doctrinal or fiscal monograph; use for spatial/institutional framing rather than contested causal closure
